settings.description:
Hoops aren’t like shoes, where you’ll stay with just one size, give or take a little.

Style and skill play largely into which hoops you select for your dance, performance, or practice mood.

settings.title: experimentation is key
settings.description: Selecting a Hoop Size is a cross-section of your current skill level, your height/size, and the tricks and flow you want to play with on this hoop. This comes down to your current experience and projected goals with your hooping.

The larger & heavier a hoop is, the more slowly it will travel around your body.

The slower movement gives more time to feel where the hoop is making contact, & to react.

Smaller hoops move faster around the body.

Smaller/lighter hoops are more challenging, as the smaller circumference requires more skill to keep the hoop up & spinning.

As you progress you’ll naturally become better using smaller sizes, either from extra practice, or just naturally familiarizing with hooping.

Exploring different hooping styles needs different kinds of hoops.

It’s common for hoopers to have several hoop sizes and types of hoops as their hooping journey progresses.

A variety of hoops by weight and size allows you to experiment with different flow styles and hooping moods.

settings.title: Hooping styles evolve over time
settings.description:
but can also change from minute to minute if you’re experimenting with new moves, or just discovering a new groove when hooping to music, or getting in some solid practice time.

You may start a flow session with a song or rhythm that changes halfway through and decide to switch to a different hoop.

—————-

Swap to a smaller size or weight hoop to be able to move and respond faster to changes.

Swap to larger hoop to find a slower and easier rhythm that allows you to relax more and jam to the music.

settings.title: How to measure for a Beginner
settings.description:
Measure vertically from the floor approximately to your navel or the top of your hip bone.

If you have a larger body size you will want a slightly bigger hoop.

If you have a smaller body size you will want a slightly smaller hoop.

settings.title: HDPE vs. Polypro Tubing for LED Hoops
settings.description:
When it comes to choosing the best tubing for your LED hoop, we strongly recommend HDPE as the default option—and here’s why:

🧪 HDPE Tubing (Default for all Moodhoops LED Hoops)
  • Material: Durable, impact-absorbing plastic
  • Appearance: Milky-white, diffused finish
  • Why we love it: HDPE is flexible, resilient, and handles impacts well—perfect for hoops with internal electronics like LEDs and batteries.
  • Recommended for: Most LED hoop users, especially if you’re unsure or using thinner tubing like 5/8″.
🔮 Polypro Tubing
  • Material: Rigid, bouncy plastic
  • Appearance: Clear and transparent
  • Why some choose it: Its stiffness gives a crisper feel and sharper lines in movement, especially appreciated by experienced flow artists.

However, polypro has some drawbacks—especially for LED hoops:

  • It’s more brittle, making it prone to cracking on impact or when flexed too much.
  • Polypro tubing becomes even more fragile in cold weather.
  • The added weight of internal components (LEDs, batteries, connectors) increases the risk of breakage.
  • Common hoop moves like breaks, reversals, or even normal use can cause stress fractures in polypro tubing.
  • High-impact hits or landing on your hoop (like during jump-throughs) can also lead to cracks.

💡 Final Tip

If you’re unsure about going with polypro and want peace of mind, HDPE is the safer, more durable choice—especially in thinner tubing sizes like 5/8″. It offers excellent performance while helping protect your investment from accidental damage.

settings.title: Hooping Moves & Style
settings.description:
Your hooping style is a combination of the types of moves you enjoy and the speed at which you like to hoop. Whether you’re into slow, meditative movement or fast-paced, technical flow, your style is shaped by how you interact with the hoop.

On-body Hooping

Also known as core hooping, this style includes any movement where the hoop is spinning around your body—typically at the waist, chest, shoulders, or legs. It’s often rhythmic and meditative, helping to build coordination, balance, and core strength.

Off-body Hooping

Off-body hooping involves moves where the hoop is no longer spinning around your core. Instead, you’re manipulating the hoop with your hands, arms, feet, ankles, or elbows. These tricks are more dynamic and often involve tosses, isolations, and quick direction changes.

Blending On-body and Off-body

Many hoopers enjoy combining both styles for a more expressive flow. Transitions between on-body and off-body moves allow for creative choreography and personal expression, and can make your hoop dance feel more fluid and dynamic.

settings.title: How Moodhoops Are Measured
settings.description:
All Moodhoops are measured by outer diameter (OD)—that’s the distance across the widest part of the hoop, including the tubing.

We offer a variety of sizes and tubing styles to match your flow. Most of our regular hoops come in 3/4″ tubing, which offers a sturdy feel and is great for hoop sizes up to 38″ OD.

For smaller hoop sizes under 33″ OD, we also offer 5/8″ tubing, which is lighter, more flexible, and perfect for faster moves, isolations, and a more responsive feel.

Because 5/8″ tubing is thinner, it holds its shape best in smaller hoop diameters. Making larger hoops with it can cause them to warp or become misshapen.

On the flip side, 3/4″ tubing is a bit too thick for very small hoops and can put too much pressure on the internal connection—especially in LED hoops.

For LED Mini Hoops, some sizes are available only in 5/8″, while others are offered in both 5/8″ and 3/4″.

Each hoop tubing uses a different size battery, so it’s important to make sure you’re selecting the right size battery for your hoop.

  • 5/8″ Moodhoops use the AAA-sized 10440 battery
  • 3/4″ FutureHoops use the AAA sized 10440 battery
  • 3/4″ PixelHoops & Classic Moodhoops use the AA sized 14500 battery

LED Moodhoops use only one battery at a time, but we definitely recommend getting additional batteries so you can glow all night long 🙂 Moodhoops use specialty lithium-ion batteries that need extra care and caution.

Check out our Battery Safety and Care information page, it’s chock full of important information about proper use of these specialty batteries.

🌀New to hooping? Welcome! 💫 If you’re just getting started or enjoy slower, flowier movement, a larger hoop is the perfect place to begin.

Our Beginner Hoops come in 39″ (Large) and 42″ (Extra Large) sizes and are ideal for:

  • Learning on-body moves like waist hooping and building muscle memory for new tricks
  • Developing a slower, more meditative flow while strengthening your core
  • Anyone who wants a hoop with extra momentum and more time to react during movement

Why Bigger Hoops Are Beginner-Friendly

Larger hoops have more space inside the circle and a bit of added weight, which means:

  • Slower rotation gives you more time to feel the hoop’s contact with your body and respond smoothly
  • Extra momentum helps keep the hoop spinning, making it easier to keep up while you learn
  • A gentler pace lets you focus on control, breath, and grounding your movement

Bonus: A Great Workout

The extra weight in large hoops adds light resistance, which naturally engages your core muscles while hooping. Waist hooping with a slower, heavier hoop can feel calming and rhythmic — great for both exercise and relaxation.

🎨 Style + Function

Our Taped Beginner Hoops are crafted with:

  • A hand-picked mix of vibrant, colorful tapes
  • Slightly heavier tubing that breaks down into smaller travel-friendly segments
  • Two beginner-friendly sizes: 39″ and 42″

🔄 Ready to Level Up?

Once you’ve mastered the basics, you might want to size down to a smaller, lighter hoop. Smaller hoops spin faster  and respond more quickly to movement, making them great for off-body tricks and dynamic flow.

settings.title: Smaller and lighter hoops
settings.description:
Once you’ve been hooping a while and have started to work up skill, or if you like to dance fast, you may want a (medium) 36 inch hoop or smaller. The smaller 36 inch hoop lends itself to a more varied mixture of on body and off body hooping. The 3/4″ thick tubing holds up well to breaks and reversals, while still being light enough to keep from getting fatigued too quickly.

Once you’ve logged lots of hooping hours, you’ll start to notice hooping with a bigger hoop becomes more difficult as you try to quickly transition from one trick to another.

Smaller hoops ranged 33 inches and below may not ideal for sustained spinning for a beginner but are perfect for transitioning back and forth from core hooping and off-body hoop dancing, which is a key component in saving strength during long dance sessions.

Hoops sized 33 inches and below come in both ultra-thin 5/8″ featherweight tubing and in 3/4″ tubing allowing you to fine tune your hoop’s specs to your hooping style as it evolves.

settings.title: Mini Hoops
settings.description:
Minis come in sizes ranging from 18″ to 23″ and are generally dual-wielded and used to do weaves and other poi-style or fan-style moves. You can also perform lots of sophisticated isolations with one or two minis.

We offer mini hoops as Polypro dayhoops, Classic Mini hoops, and FutureHoop Minis.

Check out our Tutorials page for some great Multiple Hooping tutorial videos to help you progress with minis and double hooping!

settings.title: Fire Hoop Sizing
settings.description:
Fire Wicks will add about 5 inches to each end past the tubing, for a total of 10 inches added to the clearance of your hoop. For this reason a hoop sized slightly smaller may be a good option for choosing a Fire Hoop size.

Since the Fire Wicks are removable you can choose any hoop size to add to your current hoop collection. If this hoop will be mainly for fire hooping, it’s good to select a hoop size that you’re comfortable with already.

The Fire Wicks are removable and can fit on 3/4″-7/8″ or 5/8″ tubing. Fire Hoops get your choice of a standard size HDPE hoop, which can also be upgraded to Polypro in any color! You can also add decorative hoop tape to make your hoop sparkle in the fire light!

settings.title: Hoop Grip
settings.description:
Hoop tubing with no grip added (like sandpaper, grip tape, or hoop wax) is very slick and can be difficult to keep up, even for an experienced hooper. Don’t be discouraged though! Adding grip along the inner ring of the hoop is the first place to start, but you can also add grip to the outside of your hoop to get a fuller contact.

Our LED hoops with a layer of Hoop Wax added for good grip. Hoop Wax is a transparent and lightweight solution to excellent hoop grip. Add an extra Hoop Wax heart to your cart so you can keep reapplying.

Hoop wax is an inexpensive way to get a clear film of grip on your hoop tubing. Reapply the grip wax as needed, or scrape it off to apply a different grip method. The more wax applied to your hoop the better it sticks! This stuff is really amazing!

3M grip tape is a clear silicone tape that helps your hoop keep contact with any surface. We offer this tape in different length increments. You can get rolls of the 1/3″ grip tape in 15 ft and 30 ft lengths! 10 feet of tape is just enough to do the inner ring for hoops 38″ and smaller.
We also offer1/2″ and 1″ grip tape(gaffer tape) in a rainbow of colors! This tape makes a great color accent, whether used on the inner ring of an LED hoop, or twirled around the hoop tubing.

settings.text:
Sandpaper is another effective and inexpensive way to add grip to your hoop. Using 100 grit or 80 grit sandpaper along the inner ring, or even all around the hoop tubing, add grooves into the hoop, which gives more surface area and texture for your hands, clothes, and body to make contact with.

It’s important to note that, once your tubing is sanded, grip tapes may not stick as well to just the inner ring of the tubing. Grip tape may instead need to be wrapped around the length of the hoop in a large spiral so there’s plenty of surface area for the tape to adhere to.
Please contact us if you have any questions, we are always happy to help!
